nodes.question: Does the edited image show the source mug moved to the right of the headphones, rather than merely adding a mug there while the source mug remains at its former position?
nodes.criteria: Compare the source and edited images to identify the source mug and determine whether that mug is now visibly to the right of the headphones. Pass only when the source mug's moved position is supported by the visual evidence; fail when it is clear the source mug was not moved to the right; unknown when object identity, movement, or relative position cannot be determined reliably. Do not treat an additional mug on the right alone as proof that the requested move occurred.
nodes.binding: The mug visible in the source image (blue, left of the headphones) and the headphones in the source and edited images; compare the source mug's identity and position across images.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The node correctly detects that the source mug’s former position still contains a blue blur and that a mug appears to the headphones’ right, so its fail is supported by the visual evidence; there is no transport, schema, or dependency failure. The reference “partial” is an aggregate constraint, not proof that this move check should pass: the image shows no clear evidence that the original mug was moved, and unrelated changes cannot count as progress on this requirement. Keep the source-object identity and anti-addition check, but make the criterion distinguish a clearly retained source mug from an ambiguous residual/blur: use unknown when the former-position evidence cannot reliably establish retention or identity, rather than treating a blur as conclusive. Do not force partial or lower confidence merely to match the reference; investigate whether another requirement accounts for aggregate partial. The current trace is high-confidence and specific, so avoid weakening it absent evidence that its visual interpretation is unreliable.

This supports that a mug was added on the right rather than the source mug being moved there.
